publications.title: An Assistive Sensory-Based System for Integrated Fall and Obstacle Detection
publications.subtitle: IEEE
publications.description: Traditional walking canes have offered limited mobility to elderly individuals, while leaving critical safety gaps in spatial awareness and emergency response. This paper presents a novel integrated assistive system that combines obstacle detection, fall detection, biometric monitoring, and sustainable energy harvesting in a single low-cost device, helping to minimize falls in seniors without compromising comfort. The system utilizes ultrasonic sensors with haptic feedback to give the user ample time to respond to obstacles and uneven surfaces with an accuracy of 97.75% ± 1.2% (agreement with a meter-stick baseline) up to 1.5 meters and 100% detection across 27 simulated fall trials. Alongside the hardware, the companion mobile application enables real-time pulse monitoring for the user and comprehensive emergency response capabilities for caregivers. If a fall is detected by the built-in gyroscope, the location is automatically recorded in the mobile app, and an emergency call is placed to emergency services or a family member. A thermoelectric energy harvesting system converts body heat from the user’s palm into electrical energy, sustainably powering two LEDs controlled by a switch. Comprehensive testing validates the effective delivery of haptic feedback and the reliable performance of sensors with a user-adjustable detection range. Results are preliminary from bench/lab simulations; future development includes expanded user testing and baseline comparisons.

projects.title: An Assistive Sensory-Based System for Integrated Fall and Obstacle Detection
projects.description: Worked in a 3-member team for 8 months to design an eco-friendly smart cane system for seniors with terrain profiling, fall detection, pulse tracking, and a caretaker mobile app. Integrated ultrasonic sensors, thermoelectric generators, Bluetooth module, haptic motors, gyroscope, pulse sensor into a cohesive system.- Earned Alameda County Science & Engineering Fair 1st category award among 200+ projects. Evaluated across 3 rounds by panels of judges for technical rigor and oral defense. Selected as 1 of 15 projects advancing to CSEF.- Drafted and filed a provisional patent.- Co-authored research paper on "An Assistive Sensory-Based System for Integrated Fall and Obstacle Detection". Selected for presentation and publication at IEEE-sponsored COSITE 2025. Serving as presenting author to deliver findings virtually at the conference in December 2025.

projects.title: Breathe App
projects.description: Inspired by personal struggles with asthma, developed Breathe, an Android app using Javascript, Node.js and Expo for logging respiratory symptoms and tracking triggers based on weather data. Optimized API calls for daily weather data, conducted beta testing with 20 users, and published app to the Google Play Store.
